caption: A dog walks through an office with motion-sensor lights, and the ceiling panels switch on ahead of it and go off behind it.

sa.check: A dog walks through an office with ceiling lights.
The ceiling panels switch on ahead of it.
The lights respond to the dog's movement: no one touches a switch.

pc.expect: Each panel lights as the dog approaches and its patch of floor brightens.
pc.fail: Panels light far from the dog; or stay dark as it passes beneath; or the floor stays dark under a lit panel.

pc.expect: Panels behind the dog go dark after a delay and do not flicker.
pc.fail: They stay lit indefinitely; or go off before the dog has passed; or flicker.

pc.expect: The lighting follows the dog's path.
pc.fail: Panels light in a pattern unrelated to the dog; or the dog jumps position; or lights come on with the dog gone.

pc.expect: The dog's shadow falls away from the lit panel above.
pc.fail: It points toward the panel; or in several directions; or there is none.
A panel vanishes; or appears; or the dog duplicates.
Desks rearrange; or the panels change colour; or the dog changes.

note: The dog is self-driven; only the lights' response to its position is judged. Illumination: the on/off causality of electric lights belongs to Electricity; here only where the light goes once it exists is judged.
